approach: In check_and_verify (run/mod.rs), replace the unconditional routing::NoCi with a new Athena::with_ci_source. It picks the CI source and its wait together. A nested run, or an origin that is not an https URL on github.com, gets NoCi with one read and no sleep. Any other origin gets a gh::GhClient over gh::GhCli reading the push run on athena/ci/<job id> through client.ci_source(&gh::ci_branch(job)). It is polled every 20 s for the new [budget] ci_wait_s (default 1500). routing.rs gains run_routed_with_record, which also returns the CiRecord when the result came from CI, and Paced, a CiSource wrapper that sleeps through an injected sleeper between reads. ci_result.rs stays untouched, so resolve gets pause ZERO and Paced does the pacing. The record becomes verify::reuse_statement(record, candidate), and verification.rs adds it to the verifier's check list as a "not a check" entry. Green skips local checks, red fails with the named check and no local run, and missing, cancelled, timed-out and unfinished runs fall back to local checks, all inside the existing resolve. A resumed job takes the recorded_checks branch and carries no statement. Tests drive Athena::go with a gh::Runner fake and a sleeper fake installed through a new test-only ci_seam beside check_seam, plus the existing early_seam and check_seam. With no ci_seam installed, test builds use NoCi, so existing github-origin tests never reach the real gh. No at-sign text is written anywhere: URLs are https://github.com/owner/repo, and the userinfo split in client.rs uses the escape '\u{40}'. Criterion 11 is shown by the three Athena checks; its demonstration names the seam (the existing github-origin tests run through Athena::go with early_seam and check_seam, and absent ci_seam means NoCi) and what fails without the behavior.

decisions.choice: Pace the wait in routing.rs with a Paced CiSource wrapper (sleeps through an injected &dyn Fn(Duration) before every read after the first); pass Wait{polls, pause: ZERO} to resolve.
decisions.reason: ci_result.rs is out of scope and read_ci calls std::thread::sleep directly. The wrapper makes the wait observable and fast in tests (a fake sleeper records 20 s steps) and leaves the SHA rules and the read-count logic untouched.

rejected.option: Add a sleeper parameter to ci_result::resolve/read_ci
rejected.why: ci_result.rs is not a deliverable and its rules are out of scope.

rejected.option: Real sleeping with a tiny test-only pause
rejected.why: It cannot show the 20 s step or the 75 sleeps, and it makes the timed-out test depend on wall time.

decisions.choice: Choose source and wait in one function, Athena::with_ci_source(job, wait_s, act), which hands a &dyn CiSource and a Wait to a closure.
decisions.reason: Keeps the choice atomic (no GitHub origin can never get a wait) and solves the borrow of the runner and client, which live only inside the function. Criterion 6 can Grep with_ci_source.

rejected.option: Return a boxed source plus a Wait
rejected.why: CiBranchSource borrows a GhClient that borrows the runner, so returning it needs self-referential ownership.
That keeps the unconditional-call shape being removed and splits the source/wait decision.

decisions.choice: Add pub(crate) https_origin_repository(url) to gh/client.rs, with the userinfo split written as '\u{40}'. Use it in with_ci_source.
decisions.reason: github_repository and https_github_repository in gh/early.rs are private, and early.rs is kept unchanged. The escape keeps an at-sign out of the diff (criterion 9).

rejected.why: It edits a file the brief keeps unchanged and is not a deliverable.
It accepts ssh forms and any URL containing github.com, so a lookalike path would be treated as GitHub.

decisions.choice: Add run_routed_with_record returning (Vec<CheckRun>, Option<CiRecord>); keep run_routed as a thin wrapper.
decisions.reason: The verifier statement needs the record's run address, steps and duration, which CheckRuns do not carry. The wrapper leaves the existing run_routed unit tests unchanged.

rejected.option: Rebuild the statement from the CheckRun notes
rejected.why: It would not be verify::reuse_statement, and the record fields are not all kept in the notes.
It touches every existing routing test for no gain.

decisions.choice: Test-only ci_seam module in run/mod.rs next to check_seam (thread-local runner and sleeper, install returns a Guard). Not installed means NoCi in test builds.
decisions.reason: gh/mod.rs (home of early_seam) is kept unchanged. Existing github-origin tests (run/tests.rs ci_run, run_pin_tests.rs early_run) keep passing with no edit and no network.

rejected.option: Extend early_seam to carry a Runner
Edit every existing github-origin test to install a runner
rejected.why: run_pin_tests.rs is not a deliverable, and a missed one would call the real gh.

decisions.choice: ci_wait_s is #[serde(default = ...)] (1500) in Budget, and athena.toml sets 1500 explicitly. Polls = ci_wait_s / 20 + 1; 0 gives one read.
decisions.reason: Fixtures and older configs without the field still load (Budget has deny_unknown_fields and all other fields are required). The explicit athena.toml value satisfies criterion 7. 1500 s gives 76 reads and 75 sleeps of 20 s.

rejected.why: Every config literal in tests and fixtures would break.

decisions.choice: Leave verify.rs unchanged unless a doc line needs fixing.
decisions.reason: reuse_statement already returns the text for the same SHA only and is tested. Only verification.rs needs to carry its output.

files.purpose: Add Athena::with_ci_source (source and wait together), a test-only ci_seam beside check_seam, and the check_and_verify change: call run_routed_with_record, build the reuse statement, print one ci line when a result is reused.
Add CI_POLL (20 s), ci_polls, the Paced CiSource wrapper and run_routed_with_record (run_routed stays as a wrapper), with unit tests; update the module doc that says no result is read.
Add pub(crate) https_origin_repository(url), using an escape for the userinfo split; no identity or remote text of the user-at-host form.
Add reuse: Option<String> to Checked and push a 'not a check' entry holding the statement onto the verifier's checks.
Add ci_wait_s: u64 to Budget with serde default 1500; fix any Budget literals; add load tests.
Set ci_wait_s = 1500 under [budget] with a one-line comment (listed deliverable). email_allow unchanged.
Add the CiReplies runner fake, a sleeper fake, the ci_reuse_run helper and the tests for green, red, fallbacks, no-origin and the verifier statement.
Only shared helpers if needed (such as JSON builders for a push run and a jobs reply); skip if run/tests.rs helpers suffice.
Unreleased entry for the change, including that a resumed job carries no reuse statement. No at-sign.
Expected to need no change; touched only for a doc line if reuse_statement's comment is wrong once it has a caller.

steps: Grep 'Budget {' and 'budget' in crates/ for struct-literal constructions and fixture TOMLs, so the new field does not break any.

config.rs: add pub ci_wait_s: u64 with #[serde(default = "default_ci_wait_s")] (1500) and the default fn. Add tests: the repo athena.toml loads with 1500; a budget table without the field loads with 1500. athena.toml: add ci_wait_s = 1500 with a comment under [budget].

gh/client.rs: add pub(crate) fn https_origin_repository(url: &str) -> Option<String>: trim, require the https:// prefix, take the authority, drop userinfo with rsplit_once('\u{40}'), require host == HOST, then return parse_remote(url).ok().map(|(_, r)| r). Add a unit test for the forms in no_github_origin_pushes_no_ci_branch plus a credential form built from string pieces. run/mod.rs: add test-only ci_seam (thread-local runner and sleeper, install returns a Guard, current() returns an Option) next to check_seam.

routing.rs: add pub const CI_POLL (20 s), pub fn ci_polls(wait_s) -> u32 (wait_s / 20 + 1), and pub struct Paced (inner &dyn CiSource, sleeper &dyn Fn(Duration), Cell read count) whose fetch sleeps before every read after the first. Refactor run_routed into run_routed_with_record returning (Vec<CheckRun>, Option<CiRecord>) (Some only when the record came from CI, green or red); keep run_routed as a wrapper. Add unit tests: 76 reads and 75 sleeps for 1500; one read and no sleep for 0 and for NoCi; record returned for green and red, None for a local fallback. Fix the module doc.

run/mod.rs: add Athena::with_ci_source(&self, job, wait_s, act: impl FnOnce(&dyn CiSource, Wait) -> T) -> T. Nested run, or https_origin_repository of the origin URL is None: act(&NoCi, Wait{1, ZERO}). Otherwise pick the runner (the seam in test builds, and NoCi if none is installed; GhCli in production), build GhClient::new(runner, repo) and the sleeper (seam, or std::thread::sleep), wrap client.ci_source(&crate::gh::ci_branch(job)) in Paced, and call act with Wait{polls: ci_polls(wait_s), pause: ZERO}.

run/mod.rs check_and_verify: call with_ci_source(&id, jc.config.budget.ci_wait_s, |ci, wait| run_routed_with_record(&route, &c, &changed_for_skip, ci, &exec, wait))? in place of the NoCi call. Remove the 'No candidate commit is pushed yet' comment, and print one ci line (result reused from the run address) when a CI record came back. Build reuse = record.and_then(|r| verify::reuse_statement(&r, &c)); it stays None on the recorded_checks (resumed) and nested branches. Pass it in Checked.

verification.rs: add reuse: Option<String> to Checked and destructure it. After the checks are mapped into inputs.checks, push CheckResultView { name: "ci-result", command: "not a check", passed: true, detail: statement } when it is Some, as the gap entries already do.

run/tests.rs: add CiReplies (implements gh::Runner; parses head_sha and branch from the repos/.../actions/runs path and replies with a push run of workflow ci for that sha and branch for the scenario Green, Red (clippy fails), Missing, Cancelled, TimedOut or Unfinished; replies to .../runs/<id>/jobs with the matching jobs reply; counts calls) and a sleeper fake that records durations. Add ci_reuse_run(origin, scenario), built from the pieces of ci_run, which installs early_seam, ci_seam and a recording check_seam before go and keeps the Guards alive through go. Add the five tests from the demonstrations and run them.
CHANGELOG.md: add an Unreleased entry (see criterion 10). No at-sign anywhere.

Before finishing, scan the diff for an at-sign and user-at-host forms (Grep for the at-sign over changed files, ignoring pre-existing lines). Then run cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings and cargo test --locked. Also run cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus as a no-regression check; no reading or refusal rule changes.

risks.risk: An at-sign appears somewhere in the diff, which admission refuses (the fault of the earlier job). Existing code uses '@' in early.rs, and copying it would add one.
risks.mitigation: Use '\u{40}' in client.rs, build any credential test URL from string pieces, use only https://github.com/owner/repo in CHANGELOG and tests, and run the diff scan in the last step.

risks.risk: Existing github-origin tests (run/tests.rs ci_run, run_pin_tests.rs early_run) could reach the real gh or sleep 1500 s.
risks.mitigation: In test builds with_ci_source uses NoCi when no ci_seam is installed; production never compiles the seam. The full cargo test --locked run covers it.

risks.risk: The fake runner echoes the requested sha, so the stale-SHA rule is not exercised by these tests.
risks.mitigation: The stale-run rule is covered in ci_result.rs tests, which stay unchanged. The fake only emulates the server's head_sha filter; the decision stays in production resolve.

risks.risk: https_origin_repository duplicates early.rs's private check and the two could drift.
risks.mitigation: The no-origin test asserts the same forms for push and CI read. Follow-up (make early.rs call it) is listed in open_questions.

risks.risk: A real run is 'unusable' when the aggregate job is cancelled or times out; the runner treats that as no result and waits no longer.
risks.mitigation: That is the existing parse_ci_run and resolve behavior (falls back to local checks); cancelled and timed-out are tested through go.

risks.risk: A new required Budget field would break fixture configs.
risks.mitigation: The serde default of 1500 keeps them loading, and step 1 greps Budget literals.

risks.risk: clippy -D warnings flags new items (unused ci_seam parts, too many arguments, needless borrow).
risks.mitigation: Mark ci_seam #[cfg(test)] throughout, keep argument counts small via the closure, and run clippy before finishing.

demonstrations.method: Test ci_reuse_green_skips_local_checks in run/tests.rs drives Athena::go with origin https://github.com/owner/repo. A CiReplies runner fake returns a green push run, echoing head_sha and branch from the request path as the server filter would. Asserts the recording executor was called zero times and the recorded check notes name the CI run address and the candidate SHA.
demonstrations.observes: Zero local check calls; every recorded check note names the CI run; the job proceeds to the verifier and lands.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without with_ci_source the call still passes NoCi, so the fake runner is never asked, the recording executor is called for fmt, clippy and test, and the notes do not name CI.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point Athena::go (reaches check_and_verify and with_ci_source). Guards: origin must be an https github.com URL, not a nested run. Fakes: gh::early_seam::install(fake, fake) (exists, gh/mod.rs), check_seam::install with a recording closure (exists, run/mod.rs), ci_seam::install(runner, sleeper) with a gh::Runner fake (ci_seam added in plan step 3, fake in step 8). The fake supplies only JSON; the SHA match, run choice and reuse stay in production resolve.

demonstrations.method: Test ci_reuse_red_fails_without_local_checks: the runner fake returns a failed push run whose jobs reply has clippy failing and the aggregate job failing. Same three fakes through Athena::go. Asserts the state is not Landed, the checks output and recorded check records name clippy as failed, the recording executor was called zero times, and the sleeper recorded no sleep.
demonstrations.observes: Job not landed; failing check clippy named; zero local check calls.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the CI read, local checks run and pass in the recording fake, so the job lands and the executor count is non-zero.
demonstrations.seam: Same as criterion 1: Athena::go, early_seam (exists), check_seam recording fake (exists), ci_seam runner fake with red JSON (steps 3 and 8).

demonstrations.method: Test ci_reuse_falls_back_to_local_checks, one go run per scenario: empty workflow_runs, cancelled aggregate job, conclusion timed_out, and a run in_progress on every read. Each asserts the recording executor ran fmt, clippy and test, the runner fake was called, and the job lands. For the never-finishing run it asserts 75 sleeps of 20 s and 76 reads on the fakes.
demonstrations.observes: Local checks run as before in all four cases; the job proceeds; the wait bound of 1500 s shows through the fake sleeper with no real sleeping.
demonstrations.fails_without: A fallback bug (a non-green run treated as a pass, or the job failed when no result exists) would change the executor counts and state. Without a CI read the cases cannot be told from NoCi, so the runner-fake call count is asserted too.
demonstrations.seam: Athena::go; early_seam (exists), check_seam recording fake (exists), ci_seam runner and sleeper fakes (steps 3 and 8). The 75 and 76 come from production routing::Paced and ci_polls (step 4); the fake only returns JSON and records sleeps.

demonstrations.method: Test ci_reuse_no_github_origin_uses_no_ci loops the origin forms of the existing no_github_origin_pushes_no_ci_branch test (none, local path, lookalike path containing github.com, https://gitlab.example.com/owner/repo, https://example.com/github.com/owner/repo). Each go run installs a counting runner fake and a counting sleeper fake. A routing unit test checks NoCi with a one-poll wait does one read and no sleep.
demonstrations.observes: Runner calls 0 and sleeper calls 0 for every form; local checks run once; the job lands.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the CI source were chosen without checking the origin, the fake runner would record a call or the sleeper would record sleeps for the none, local-path, lookalike and other-host origins.
demonstrations.seam: Athena::go; early_seam (exists); check_seam recording fake (exists); ci_seam counting fakes (steps 3 and 8). It also covers https_origin_repository (step 3).

demonstrations.method: Test ci_reuse_statement_reaches_the_verifier_input: the green setup with an agent script wrapping counting(...) as the existing retry test in run/tests.rs does, to capture spec.user_prompt when spec.role is Verifier. Asserts the prompt contains verify::reuse_statement(&record, candidate) built from the same CiRecord and the candidate SHA read from the CI branch push recorded on the EarlyFake.
demonstrations.observes: The verifier prompt contains the statement naming the CI run address, the candidate SHA and the step results.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the Checked.reuse entry in verification.rs, the verifier prompt has no such text and the contains assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Athena::go; existing athena_with and counting script (exists); the fakes of criterion 1 (steps 3 and 8). The expected string comes from calling production verify::reuse_statement (exists), not from copied logic in a fake.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff of run/mod.rs and Grep with_ci_source over crates/. Check the run_routed call no longer takes a literal NoCi, with_ci_source returns NoCi or the GitHub source together with the Wait, and the candidate &c is still passed as the SHA.
demonstrations.observes: with_ci_source is defined once and called from check_and_verify; the only NoCi mention is inside it for the no-origin and nested branch; the SHA argument is the candidate commit.

demonstrations.method: Config tests: a new assertion that Config loaded from the repository athena.toml has budget.ci_wait_s == 1500, and that a budget table without the field loads with 1500. Read the diff of athena.toml and config.rs.
demonstrations.observes: athena.toml has ci_wait_s = 1500 under [budget]; Budget has pub ci_wait_s: u64 with the serde default; existing config load tests pass.

demonstrations.method: Grep early_seam::install and ci_seam::install in run/tests.rs and check each new https github.com test reaches both through the single helper ci_reuse_run, which also installs the check_seam recorder. No test installs GhCli or Command; ci_seam is #[cfg(test)] only.
demonstrations.observes: Every new github-origin test goes through a helper that installs the early fakes, the runner and sleeper fakes and the check fake before go; with no runner installed the path uses NoCi, so no test reaches the network.

demonstrations.method: Scan the added lines of the whole diff with Grep for an at-sign and user-at-host forms, including gh/client.rs, athena.toml, CHANGELOG.md and tests. New URLs are https://github.com/owner/repo; the userinfo split is '\u{40}'. The producer runs the same scan before finishing.
demonstrations.observes: No added line contains an at-sign form; athena.toml email_allow is unchanged.

demonstrations.method: Read the new Unreleased CHANGELOG entry.
demonstrations.observes: The entry says the checks stage reads the push run on athena/ci/<job id>; green skips local checks; red fails; missing, cancelled, timed-out or unfinished runs fall back; [budget] ci_wait_s is 1500 polled every 20 s; the reuse statement reaches the verifier; a resumed job carries no reuse statement. No at-sign.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks Athena runs on the result: cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings, and cargo test --locked (the last is the named command; the verifier runs the other two as whole simple commands too). The test run includes every new test and every existing github-origin test (ci_run in run/tests.rs, early_run in run_pin_tests.rs, the config load tests and the routing unit tests).
demonstrations.observes: fmt reports no diff, clippy reports no warnings (no unused Paced or ci_seam item, no needless clone), and every test passes. Existing github-origin tests with no ci_seam installed see NoCi, so none sleeps 1500 s or calls the real gh.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the behavior were missing or broken, cargo test --locked fails: the new green, red, fallback, no-origin and verifier-statement tests fail, config load tests fail if ci_wait_s is missing from athena.toml or the schema, and existing github-origin tests fail or hang if with_ci_source reached the real gh or a real 1500 s wait when no ci_seam is installed. cargo fmt --check fails on unformatted new code, and clippy -D warnings fails on warnings in it.
demonstrations.seam: The cargo commands are the entry points; they run the test suite, whose tests call production Athena::go. Seams used: gh::early_seam::install and check_seam::install (both exist, read in gh/mod.rs and run/mod.rs), and ci_seam::install with the CiReplies runner and recording sleeper fakes (ci_seam added in plan step 3, fakes in step 8). With no ci_seam installed, test builds use NoCi (step 5), which is how the existing tests stay offline. The fakes supply JSON replies and record calls only; the decision logic is production code.

open_questions: Is check_and_verify's &c always a full 40-hex SHA? If not, resolve returns BadSha and run_routed falls back to local checks (safe but silent). I did not check how built.commit is produced.

I did not read crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs. The plan adds no reading, plan or refusal rule (the origin check is a URL matcher for the CI read only), so no corpus case is mapped; the producer runs the corpus test only as a regression check.
Should early.rs's https_github_repository delegate to the new https_origin_repository once a job may edit early.rs? Out of scope here.
verify.rs is a listed deliverable but needs no change in this plan; the producer may leave it untouched.

Whether the red-CI job state is Rejected or Failed depends on existing verdict code. The red test should assert not Landed and the failing check's name; the producer reads the actual state and asserts it.
